sentences.text: Rivian went from no revenue in FY2020 to $5,387 million in FY2025, a 48.1% three-year CAGR from FY2022 [F2][F7][D342].
The step change came in FY2022, when revenue jumped 2914.5% to $1,658 million as deliveries began [F4][D83].
That ramp was driven by increased deliveries of 19,412 vehicles [P67].
Growth then decelerated sharply to 12.1% in FY2024 and 8.4% in FY2025 [D187][D239].
FY2025 automotive revenue fell on 9,332 fewer deliveries, partly from expiration of 45W tax credits [P22].
Software and services contributed 21.6pp of FY2025's 8.4% growth, while new electric vehicles subtracted 10.5pp [D295][D288][D239].
Software and services revenue rose 221.7% on vehicle electrical architecture and software development services for the Joint Venture [D294][P18].
Software and services reached 28.9% of revenue in FY2025 versus 9.7% in FY2024 [D293][D290].
Operating expenses grew 6.9% against revenue growth of 8.4%, so incremental operating margin was 264.7% [D258][D239][D265].
Diluted shares rose 17.1% in FY2025, so EPS improved 34.5% while net loss shrank 23.2% [D260][D242][D241].
Operating margin of -66.5% in FY2025 is the window high but still far below the -129.4% median [F31][D325][D326].
Gross margin turned positive at 2.7%, up 26.8pp, versus a -45.8% window median [F19][D252][D332].
The gross-margin gain came from higher average selling prices and lower cost per vehicle [P20].
Cost of revenue fell 15.0% on fewer vehicles produced and lower raw material and conversion costs [D255][P21].
SG&A was the one drag, costing 0.5pp as it grew 9.9% on go-to-market expansion [D269][D257].
Operating cash flow of -$779 million was -14.5% of revenue, and free cash flow of -$2,489 million was -46.2% [F64][D227][F78][D226].
The operating cash improvement was primarily driven by a significant reduction in net loss [P4].
Capex rose 49.9% to $1,710 million, or 31.7% of revenue and 2.18x D&A [D246][F71][D225][D228].
The capex increase funded expansion of production capacity at the Normal Factory [P3].
Net cash fell to $1,642 million in FY2025 from $3,259 million, with total debt flat at $4,440 million [D231][D179][D230].
The current ratio dropped to 2.33x, the window low, from a 4.94x median [F129][D339][D341].
Financing inflow of $886 million came mainly from $750 million of Class A shares issued to Volkswagen Group [F92][P2].
Diluted shares rose 17.1% in FY2025, and equity fell 30.0% to $4,594 million [D260][D249][F142].
Rivian has posted a net loss in each of the last seven years, from -$426 million in FY2019 to -$3,646 million in FY2025 [R1][F32][F38].
Stock-based compensation was 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last five years [R2][D223].
Cash and investments of $6,082 million cover only 2.4 years of the latest burn [D229][D236].
New electric vehicles were 67.6% of revenue and fell 12.5% in FY2025 [D286][D287].
Product revenue members sum to 129% of consolidated revenue, so they cannot be added [R6].
Gross margin: a print above the FY2025 level of 2.7% would confirm the cost trend, while a return below zero would reverse it [F19].
Operating cash flow: a move above the FY2025 -$779 million toward breakeven would confirm the burn trend [F64].
Software and services share: holding above the FY2025 28.9% would sustain the mix shift [D293].
